items.title: Sylvia Karpagam’s ‘The Meat of the Matter’ calls for freeing India’s plate from prejudice
items.summary: In modern India, the kitchen has become a battlefield for state-sanctioned majoritarianism. While the right to safe, nutritious food is a fundamental prerequisite for human survival, public policy under the current dispensation has weaponised dietary habits to enforce social hierarchies. From the institutional exclusion of eggs in school midday meals to targeted communal bans on meat vendors, what ends up on an Indian's plate is increasingly engineered by prejudice rather than public health science. This toxic overlap of nutrition science, state overreach, and caste bias forms the volatile core of Dr Sylvia Karpagam’s The Meat of the Matter: How the Politics of Food Shapes Our Health . In this extensively researched and cogently argued book, Dr Karpagam makes a compelling case that the health of Indians would be best served by ditching superstition and prejudice in favour of a science-driven, evidence-based approach. Essential to this enterprise is the political will to acknowledge a fact contrary to popular misconception: the vast majority of Indians are meat-eaters. items.title: ₹20 lakh bill after Rapido bike crash: Bengaluru woman’s fight for accountability
items.summary: A Rapido bike taxi ride in Bengaluru left Sani Krishna with nine broken ribs, multiple surgeries and medical bills exceeding ₹20 lakh. She says she has not received any compensation from the company so far. Sani alleges the rider tried to overtake a tractor before the bike skidded, throwing her into its path. She also says her attempts to seek help from Rapido went unanswered until she spoke publicly about the accident. Now, as she prepares to approach the consumer court, her case raises a larger question: when a passenger is seriously injured during an app-based ride, who is responsible?

items.title: Supreme Court scraps ₹425 crore penalty over fake citations, AI hallucinations in customs order
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a ₹425.28 crore customs penalty imposed on a diamond trader after finding that the adjudicating officer had relied on non-existent cases, fake citations and legal propositions hallucinated by artificial intelligence (AI). [ Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya v. Union of India and Another ] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that reliance on such dubious material was fatal to the penalty order. “ The use of AI in this case, resulting in reliance placed by the second respondent on material which is dubious, proves fatal to the sustainability of the order imposing penalty on the appellant. Such circumstances compel us to interfere and remand the case, ” the Court said. Thus, the Court set aside the penalty order passed by the Additional Commissioner of Customs, Surat as well as the Gujarat High Court order that had confirmed it. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu The case arose from an order passed by the Additional Commissioner on October 8, 2025, imposing a penalty of ₹425.28 crore on Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya under Section 114 of the Customs Act, 1962. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed all States to respond within 3 weeks to a status report submitted by Amicus Curiae highlighting vacancies in district and state consumer commissions. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed States to explain compliance with its July 22, 2026 order on pay and allowances for commission members. Pertinently, the Court also took note of a report by the President of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) on vacancies and pendency in consumer commissions. The Court said that the report submitted by the NCDRC President requires serious consideration. Key concerns raised in the report included the appointment process for commission members and the transition to a new enactment, with members under the old regime continuing only until September 6. Attorney General R Venkataramani suggested that selection processes which had begun under the old law may be completed subject to the terms and conditions prescribed under the new enactment. A meeting of the university’s general council will now likely take a decision on the matter. The cancellation of the NLSIU convocation was the fallout of developments stemming from Hyderabad NALSAR students objecting to CJI Surya Kant attending their convocation. Bar Council of India (BCI) Manan Kumar Mishra went on to threaten to prevent NALSAR students’ enrollment in the bar. At the time, NLSIU students, extending solidarity with NALSAR, had objected to the CJI and BCI chief being part of their convocation. The CJI is the chancellor of NLSIU. The BCI chairperson presides over the general council meetings. The general council is empowered to decide on broad policies and programmes of the NLSIU. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday appointed advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus curiae in a personality rights suit filed by Bollywood actor Janhvi Kapoor. The Court's appointment of Bhatia as amicus comes against the backdrop of its earlier concerns over the scope of personality rights claims. The matter was listed before Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani . During the hearing, counsel appearing for Kapoor submitted that the URLs identified as infringing had been segregated and categorised in accordance with the directions issued by the Court during an earlier hearing . The counsel also sought early consideration of the categories for the purpose of passing an interim order. Taking note of the submissions, the Court ordered, "Considering the issues involved, this court considers it appropriate to appoint advocate Gautam Bhatia as amicus to assist the court." Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani On August 11, the Court had directed the takedown of online content concerning Kapoor that was ex facie pornographic, obscene, prurient or lascivious and appeared to directly monetise her personality rights. items.title: More renewable energy disputes will fall outside regulators, go to arbitration: Gourab Banerji
items.summary: India’s rapid expansion of renewable energy will lead to a larger number of disputes falling outside electricity regulators and being resolved through arbitration, Senior Advocate Gourab Banerji has said. Banerji, President of the Arbitration Bar of India (ABI), said that while tariff disputes would necessarily remain within the regulatory framework, renewable-energy projects were generating several other categories of disputes capable of arbitration. “Because of renewable energy being such a big player, I think a large number of the disputes will now fall outside the regulator .” He cited EPC contractor disputes, supply disputes, operation and maintenance disputes, storage and performance disputes as well as shareholder disputes. Banerji said he preferred arbitration or mediation backed by technical experts rather than requiring parties to approach regulators for every dispute. “ I am actually more comfortable with arbitration plus experts or mediation plus experts as opposed to going to the regulator for each and everything .” The discussion was part of “Investing in India’s Future: Powering Growth Through Energy, Infrastructure & Legal Certainty” , held during Singapore Conventi

[Kritikal Solutions Vs Byju's K3] The direction came after the RP of another Byju's company, K3 Education, claimed that goods worth about ₹150 crore were sold for nearly ₹16 crore. A Bench of Judicial Member Sunil Kumar Aggarwal and Technical Member Radhakrishna Sreepada also impleaded successful bidder Comprint Tech Solutions (India) Private Limited as party to the proceedings. The NCLT said the ownership of several auctioned articles remained uncertain and that their preservation was necessary until evidence was produced. “ Even if part of the auctioned articles actually belonged to TLPL, the ownership of rest of the articles remains in haze, ” the order stated. The tribunal added that maintaining status quo would not prejudice any party, whereas a further change in the position of the assets could not subsequently be undone. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday directed the Delhi government to expedite the process of filling vacancies in Delhi's Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA). A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia directed the government to file an affidavit regarding the appointments in two weeks. "We direct that the process of filling up the posts be expedited...File an affidavit in two weeks...See to it that at least the judicial members are appointed," the Court said. It was stated that the Chairperson's post fell vacant on August 11, 2026, after Kumar turned 65, while a member's post has been vacant since December 2025. Jaleel said Kanthapuram’s remarks should be understood in the context of concerns among sections of the Muslim community over the conduct and positions of women associated with the Indian Union Muslim league (IUML). CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby, however, described Kanthapuram’s remarks as similar to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s (RSS) stand on women. “This is against the Indian constitution which guarantees gender equality. The controversy began after the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama, an influential Sunni Muslim scholars’ organisation led by Kanthapuram, issued a circular last week saying it was not permissible for young women to be present among unrelated men at public forums.
